item.title: Ep. 03 — A New Chairman, Deposits Outrunning Loans, And Plaid
item.description: A leadership change at Saudi Arabia's capital markets regulator has reopened the foreign-ownership question, while listed-bank deposits outgrew lending for a second straight quarter and weekly POS spending held above three and a half billion dollars on a surge in school fees. Globally: Fintech Galaxy's in-principle nod from the UAE central bank for open finance, Fitch on a three-hundred-and-twenty-billion-dollar UAE debt market, Rabobank's two-billion-euro AI commitment, and a Tokyo convenience-store chain running stablecoins through ordinary POS registers. The product spotlight is Plaid — what a bank-data network actually sells, and why the consent screen is the real product.

## Fintech Pulse Daily — Tuesday 25 August 2026
### Saudi Arabia - **CMA leadership change.** Bloomberg (24 Aug) reported that leadership changes at the capital markets regulator have revived investor and banker hopes for further liberalisation, including a long-awaited easing of foreign-ownership limits. Mazen Al-Sudairi — former head of research at Al Rajhi Bank and an adviser at the Secretariat General of the Council of Ministers — was appointed chairman. - **Bank balance sheets.** Net loans at the ten listed Saudi banks rose 7% year on year to SR3.25trn (~$865.2bn) at end-Q2 2026; deposits rose 9% to SR3.15trn. Deposit growth outpaced lending for a second consecutive quarter (Al Rajhi Capital, via Arab News). Al Rajhi Bank and SNB held the largest loan books at SR762.10bn and SR739.56bn, each up 3%; Riyad Bank and Banque Saudi Fransi each grew 7%. - **Card spending.** Weekly POS value came in at SR14.19bn (~$3.79bn) — a third straight week above $3.5bn — with education-related transactions up 62.7% week on week ahead of the school year. Q1 2026 consumer spending was SR425bn, up 6.8% year on year. - **Sukuk.** The August domestic sukuk issuance raised SR9.52bn (~$2.54bn), up 77.94% on July; the first tranche of SR1.55bn matures in 2031. - **Open banking.** SAMA began licensing fintechs to provide open banking services in March 2026 after the sandbox phase; open banking is now a fully supervised licensed activity. - **Context.** SAMA Governor Ayman Al-Sayari took up a two-year term as the Financial Stability Board's Regional Engagement Chair on 10 August 2026.
### Global - **Fintech Galaxy** received in-principle approval from the Central Bank of the UAE to operate as an open finance provider, allowing it to participate in Al Tareq, the UAE's open finance scheme. Full approval still pending. - **Fitch** put the UAE debt market at $320bn, with dollar issuance up 40%. - **Rabobank** said it will commit up to €2bn over three years to build and scale AI capabilities (Interim Results 2026). - **Visa/BioCatch** — Visa's $2.4bn all-cash deal for the Israeli behavioural fraud-prevention firm is expected to close in Q2 2027. - **Stablecoins at the till.** NETSTARS and Lawson ran a second in-store stablecoin payment trial in Tokyo, taking USDC and USDT on Solana, Morph and Polygon, and JPYC on Polygon, from MetaMask wallets through Lawson's existing POS registers via the NETSTARS Stablecoin Pay gateway. Participation was limited to company stakeholders.
### Product spotlight — Plaid What a bank-data network sells, how Link actually works from the user's side, the access-token model, where the revenue comes from (per-call data, then risk scoring and payment initiation), the fragility of screen-scraped connections, the shift to OAuth and bank-charged data access, and the competitive set. Includes the abandoned $5.3bn Visa acquisition after the DOJ's 2020 antitrust suit.
**Lesson:** where a regulator mandates access, coverage stops being a moat. The defensible product is the consent experience and the decision you make in the seconds after the connection succeeds.
### Sources - Bloomberg — Saudi capital markets shakeup: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-24/saudi-capital-markets-shakeup-puts-foreign-inflows-back-in-focus - Arab News — Saudi listed banks' net loans rise 7% to $865.2bn in Q2: https://www.arabnews.com/node/2655204/amp - Arab News — Saudi weekly consumer spending at $3.79bn as education surges: https://www.arabnews.com/node/2655399/business-economy - Arab News — Saudi Arabia raises $2.54bn in August sukuk issuance: https://www.arabnews.com/node/2655175/business-economy - Arab News — UAE debt market hits $320bn (Fitch): https://www.arabnews.com/saudiarabia - SAMA — Commences licensing of fintech companies for open banking: https://www.sama.gov.sa/en-US/MediaCenter/News/pages/news-1135.aspx - Clyde & Co — SAMA's open banking licensing framework: https://www.clydeco.com/en/insights/2026/03/sama-new-licensing-framework-for-open-banking - FinTech Futures — Fintech Galaxy secures IPA for domestic open finance services: https://www.fintechfutures.com/regulatory-actions/fintech-galaxy-ipa-approval-cbuae - Open Banking Expo — Fintech Galaxy IPA / Al Tareq: https://www.openbankingexpo.com/news/fintech-galaxy-receives-in-principle-approval-from-cbuae-to-operate-as-open-finance-provider/ - FinTech Futures — Top five fintech news stories of the week, 7 August 2026 (Visa/BioCatch, Rabobank AI): https://www.fintechfutures.com/fintech/fintech-futures-top-five-news-stories-of-the-week-7-august-2026 - FinTech Futures — August 2026: Top five AI stories of the month: https://www.fintechfutures.com/ai-in-fintech/august-2026-top-five-ai-stories-of-the-month - Mintmark Brief — Stablecoins & Tokenization, week ending 21 August 2026 (Lawson/NETSTARS): https://buttondown.com/mintmarkresearch/archive/weekly-briefing-2026-08-21/ - SAMA on X — Governor Al-Sayari appointed FSB Regional Engagement Chair: https://x.com/sama_gov

# Fintech Pulse Daily — Monday 24 August 2026
**Runtime:** ~12 minutes
## In this episode
**Cold open — tokenised equities go live.** Coinbase put tokenised shares of Apple, Nvidia, Meta and Alphabet live on Base using a purpose-built token standard, B20, with roughly 50 DeFi protocols supporting them on day one. B20 extends ERC-20 so existing wallets and routers work unchanged, and dividends and splits run through an on-chain multiplier so balances stay fixed and DeFi positions do not break. The tokens are offered under Regulation S and are not available to US persons; Robinhood's 2,000-plus stock tokens are EU/EEA only. The SEC's tokenisation "innovation exemption" remains delayed pending the Senate's 15 September CLARITY Act vote. Total RWA value on chain sat near $38.4bn on 21 August, with holders around 2.5 million — up roughly 93% over 30 days.
**Saudi.** Listed Saudi banks' net loans rose 7% to $865.2bn in Q2 — roughly three and a quarter trillion riyals. A separate earlier read put deposits near $835bn with bank credit up 7.3%; the hosts deliberately refuse to net the two figures against each other. Backdrop: SAMA has begun licensing fintech companies to provide open banking services, moving firms out of the sandbox and into supervised entity status.
**Global.** Treasury proposed the regulations implementing the GENIUS Act's central prohibition — who may issue, offer and sell payment stablecoins in the US. Issuance ban effective 18 January 2027; offer-and-sale cutoff for coins from unlicensed issuers in July 2028; comments close 19 October. Comptroller Gould has said the OCC's companion supervisory rule will be final by November. Same week: FASB proposed conditions under which a stablecoin counts as a cash equivalent on corporate balance sheets, and Standard Chartered became the first bank to distribute Hong Kong's HKDAP stablecoin.
**AI.** The Cambridge Centre for Alternative Finance's 2026 Global AI in Financial Services Report draws on 628 respondents across 151 countries. On productivity impact by function, 203 fintechs and 149 traditional FIs were surveyed: fintechs report 86% positive impact in technology, data and product against 68% for traditional FIs. Risk and compliance was the only function where traditional institutions marginally edged ahead; both groups lag in corporate functions and leadership.
## Product spotlight — Marqeta
- **What it is:** an issuer processor with an API in front of it, sitting between a programme owner and the card networks. - **What it does not remove:** the sponsor bank. Somebody still owns the BIN, the settlement account and the regulatory relationship. - **Just-in-time funding:** at authorisation, Marqeta calls the programme owner's endpoint with merchant, amount and category; the owner approves and funds the card for that exact amount inside the authorisation window. Configure the fallback — approve or decline — before you sign. - **Money:** mainly a share of interchange plus per-transaction and per-card processing fees. Thin take rate, volume business. Note the well-documented customer concentration in Block. - **Where it breaks:** markets where interchange is regulated down, and buyers who mistake a processor for a full card programme (ledger, KYC, disputes, programme management all remain yours). - **Competitors:** Galileo, Thredd, i2c, Enfuce, Pismo, Stripe Issuing, Adyen Issuing, Fiserv, FIS, NymCard, and the perennial in-house build. - **Lesson:** the authorisation became a decision point rather than a balance lookup. The card is a trigger; the product is the rules engine behind it.
## What to watch tomorrow - Comment letters into the Treasury stablecoin file ahead of the 19 October close - Week-two retention on the Coinbase tokenised equities, not launch-day protocol counts - Any Saudi bank commentary on deposit competition in the next results round
## Sources - Arab News — Saudi listed banks' net loans rise 7% to $865.2bn in Q2: https://www.arabnews.pk/node/2655204/business-economy - Arab News — Saudi bank credit rises 7.3% as deposits grow to $835bn: https://www.arabnews.com/node/2653116/amp - SAMA — SAMA commences licensing of fintech companies to provide open banking services: https://www.sama.gov.sa/en-US/MediaCenter/News/pages/news-1135.aspx - Clyde & Co — SAMA's new licensing framework for open banking: https://www.clydeco.com/en/insights/2026/03/sama-new-licensing-framework-for-open-banking - Stobox — Weekly RWA & Tokenization Digest, 19–25 August 2026 (Coinbase/B20, Standard Chartered/HKDAP, RWA totals): https://www.stobox.io/blog/rwa-tokenization-digest-aug-19-25-2026 - Mintmark Brief — Stablecoins & Tokenization, week ending 21 August 2026 (Treasury section 3, OCC, FASB, Wyoming): https://buttondown.com/mintmarkresearch/archive/weekly-briefing-2026-08-21/ - FinTech Global — FinTechs report 86% productivity gains in tech and product, 24 August 2026: https://fintech.global/2026/08/24/fintechs-report-86-productivity-gains-in-tech-and-product-revealing-an-uneven-ai-impact/ - Statista — AI productivity impact in finance by firm type, 2026: https://www.statista.com/statistics/1661246/ai-productivity-impact-in-finance-by-type/

# Tamara Becomes a Lender, Stablecoins Get Charters **Fintech Pulse Daily — Sunday 23 August 2026, Riyadh**
## In this episode
### Saudi Arabia - **Tamara Finance Company Q2 2026.** Revenue SAR 707m (~$188m), up 152% from SAR 280m a year earlier. Net profit SAR 84m, down 32% from SAR 123m in Q1, on higher funding costs and expected credit losses. The Sharia-compliant consumer-financing line produced SAR 228m of revenue, with receivables of SAR 3.14bn at end-June against SAR 3.36bn in the original pay-in-instalments book. Credit charges absorbed 27% of quarterly revenue; the Goldman Sachs / Citi / Apollo facility is reported fully drawn at ~$1.54bn. - **Tabby, same quarter.** Revenue up 21% to ~$104m; net profit down 54% to ~$3.1m. Tabby was valued at $4.5bn earlier this year. FWDstart reports both companies have shelved Tadawul listing plans for now. - **Merchant-side read.** Checkout.com data cited in market research puts the conversion lift from embedded BNPL at 20–30%; Saudi online retail rose 78.3% to SAR 37.02bn in 2024. - **Backdrop:** SAMA moved open banking out of the sandbox into a full licensing regime on 26 March 2026, with requirements covering API performance, data security, consent management and governance.
### Global - **OCC / World Liberty Financial (14 August).** Preliminary conditional approval to organise World Liberty Trust Company, N.A., a de novo national trust bank for USD1 issuance and redemption, reserve management and institutional digital-asset custody. USD1 is stated at over $4bn in circulation. Conditions include at least $20m capital (≥$10m in eligible liquid assets) and appointment of an internal audit manager. The charter would let the company issue, custody reserves and manage settlement without relying on BitGo. Conflict-of-interest criticism has been widely reported given the venture's Trump-family backing. - **Ripple / Clearpool / Cicada Partners (21 August).** An institutional credit fund that lends RLUSD to fintech and payments companies on the XRP Ledger, with Clearpool building the lending infrastructure on the ledger's proposed lending protocol. - **UK funding.** KPMG data reported by FinTech Futures shows UK fintech funding at a decade low.
### Product spotlight — Stripe Connect What it is, who it serves, the hosted onboarding flow step by step, how charges and platform fees are taken, payout control, where chargeback liability actually lands, reserves, how Stripe monetises the layer, and where it stops working (economics at scale, loss of control over risk decisions, market coverage and local licensing). Competitors discussed: Adyen for Platforms, Checkout.com, PayPal, Airwallex, Rapyd, and payfac-as-a-service from acquirers.
**Takeaway:** onboarding *is* the product — and if your acquiring pipeline is a list of merchants, the decision is being made one layer above you, in the software those merchants run on.
*Note: the Stripe Connect segment is a general product explainer. No pricing figures are quoted because published rates vary by market and by negotiated agreement.*
## Tomorrow - Any Tamara statement on new funding lines. - Names converting on SAMA's open banking licence list. - Whether other stablecoin issuers follow World Liberty into a trust-charter application.
## Sources - Tamara Q2 2026 results — entARABI: https://entarabi.com/en/2026/08/tamaras-saudi-revenue-surges-to-sar-707-million-in-q2-as-islamic-financing-nears-bnpl/ - Tabby and Tamara diverge; CMA and Saudi listings — FWDstart: https://www.fwdstart.me/p/tabby-and-tamara-diverge-in-saudi-cma-probes-the-kingdom-s-ipo-flops - Tamara Q1 2026 and Tadawul plans — FWDstart: https://www.fwdstart.me/p/tamara-q1-revenue-triples-as-islamic-financing-line-scales-from-zero-to-27-of-sales - Tamara financing package and Tabby valuation — Business Today Middle East: https://businesstoday.me/business/fintech/tamara-and-tabby-show-saudi-bnpl-has-grown-up/ - Saudi BNPL market outlook, conversion and e-commerce data: https://finance.yahoo.com/small-business/articles/saudi-arabia-buy-now-pay-154300109.html - SAMA commences licensing for open banking services: https://www.sama.gov.sa/en-US/MediaCenter/News/pages/news-1135.aspx - Analysis of SAMA's open banking licensing framework — Clyde & Co: https://www.clydeco.com/en/insights/2026/03/sama-new-licensing-framework-for-open-banking - OCC preliminary conditional approval for World Liberty Trust Company — Business Wire: https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260814578392/en/OCC-Grants-World-Liberty-Financial-Preliminary-Conditional-Approval-to-Establish-National-Trust-Bank-for-USD1-Stablecoin-Operations - Conditions and conflict-of-interest coverage: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/articles/trump-linked-world-liberty-financial-181349466.html - Weekly stablecoin and tokenisation brief (Ripple / Clearpool / Cicada, 21 August): https://buttondown.com/mintmarkresearch/archive/weekly-briefing-2026-08-21/ - Top five fintech stories of the week, 21 August 2026 — FinTech Futures: https://www.fintechfutures.com/fintech/fintech-futures-top-five-news-stories-of-the-week-21-august-2026 - UK fintech funding at decade low (KPMG data) — FinTech Futures: https://www.fintechfutures.com/
